Country.evidence_source: All the primary health centeres (nine) in Hofuf city, Saudi Arabia, were included in the study.

Sample.evidence_source: the required sample for this study was 207 women, where n is the minimum sample size, z= standard deviation score =1.96, p= prevalence of obesity 84% among Saudi middle-aged women [17], q=1-p, d= 0.05 at the 95% confidence interval. n= (1.96)2 x (0.84) x (1 - 0.84)/ (0.05)2 =207 women.

Survey method.evidence_source: This was a cross-sectional face-to-face interview design study, with the convenience sampling technique adopted to collect the samples, which included those who were consented to participate in the study.

Mean age of participants.evidence_source: Inclusion criteria stated participants were 45–65-year-old, but no mean age was reported.

Source of sample.evidence_source: All the primary health centeres (nine) in Hofuf city, Saudi Arabia, were included in the study. Subjects were approached in the waiting rooms of the health centeres.

Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: Four female student nutritionists attended a cooperative training course and they were trained to assist in the data collection with the researchers (training included interview technique and anthropometric measurements);

section_summary.extract_value: This Methods section describes a single cross-sectional, face-to-face interview study conducted over October–December 2017 using convenience sampling at nine primary health centers in Hofuf city, Saudi Arabia. The target (required) sample size was 207 women aged 45–65 years, data were collected via trained nutritionists who conducted interviews and performed anthropometric measurements; no results (e.g., mean age, BMI, racial composition, or body appreciation measures) are reported in this section.
